hero.greeting: Hello, my name is Pedro Vitor
hero.bio: I am a Computer Science student specializing in Data Science. I also study software engineering, software architecture, and system design, with the goal of eventually moving into MLOps.
hero.en_notice: Hello, and thanks for the visit. If you do not know portuguese, you can translate to english by clicking in the translate button on the menu.

rec_system.title: Recommender System
rec_system.desc: I implemented and evaluated two recommendation systems: a memory-based approach using KNN and a model-based approach using Funk's SVD. The pipeline involved dataset cleaning and organization, data normalization, model training, and performance evaluation. In the SVD-based approach, latent factors for users and items were learned to model their interactions. For both approaches, I performed hyperparameter tuning to optimize the models and compare their performance. The model achieved an RMSE of 0.8527 and a validation RMSE of 0.9313. The project includes a paper detailing the methodology, experiments, and results.

movie_rec.title: Movie Recommender System
movie_rec.desc: A simple movie recommendation system that, unlike the one described above, was built using the Scikit-learn library. The user selects the number of movies they wish to rate and assigns a score to each one. Based on this, the system recommends a list of movies the user is likely to enjoy. Two approaches were implemented: one using a "bag of words" (or "soup of words") technique and another that did not use this approach.

mini_course.title: Machine Learning Short Course
mini_course.desc: Planned and taught an introductory mini-course covering supervised learning concepts, including Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, and Clustering. The course provided a practical and instructional overview of the entire machine learning pipeline—from preprocessing to model training and evaluation—using Python and Scikit-learn. The presentation was open to the general academic community.

lin_reg.title: Linear Regression
lin_reg.desc: Iterative development of a linear regression algorithm. The data is processed, ranging from missing value checks to numerical data normalization.

nn_class.title: Classification with Neural Networks
nn_class.desc: A dense neural network system trained to solve a classification problem. The project uses a classic problem: classifying Titanic survivors. The pipeline involved data cleaning and preparation, data normalization, training combined with validation, and techniques to prevent overfitting, such as dropout.

data_analysis.title: Data Analysis
data_analysis.desc: An exploratory data analysis (EDA) was conducted using data collected by the IBGE (Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics). The aim of the study was to perform data mining to uncover hidden insights, thereby enabling better attention to cases requiring it. Data preprocessing and clustering were carried out during the analysis to facilitate a more effective examination.

assoc_rules.title: Association Rules
assoc_rules.desc: This project was analyzed using a different approach, employing association rules, such as Support, Confidence, Lift, and Conviction, to explore and discover the events and characteristics that led customers to abandon a telephone company's service (i.e., to identify the factors driving churn). In addition to association rules, the FP-Growth algorithm was used to assist in the data analysis.

clustering.title: Clustering
clustering.desc: An analysis and clustering process was performed on a dataset regarding student performance at a school to identify student profiles and examine correlations. The goal was to determine whether measures should be implemented to assist students with poor performance. Preliminary data ETL was conducted, and PCA was applied to improve the visualization of the resulting groups. The K-prototypes algorithm was selected for clustering due to its ability to handle a mix of categorical and non-categorical data.

nn_linreg.title: Neural network for mathematical representations
nn_linreg.desc: These are the "simplest" ones. I developed two neural network implementations using PyTorch to understand how the network changes and learns when adjusting parameters such as layers, neurons, and epochs and how techniques to prevent overfitting, like dropout, alter the network. These two implementations were designed for linear regression and for modeling a sine wave.

rnn.title: Recurrent Neural Network
rnn.desc: In this project, we developed an image classifier using the CIFAR-10 dataset. For validation, I employed a holdout technique, splitting the data into 80% for training, 10% for testing, and 10% for validation. To mitigate overfitting, I applied data augmentation, performing image mirroring, rotation, and normalization during training.

encoders.title: Recurrent Neural Network (Encoders)
encoders.desc: On VAEs i created an anomaly detector. So the neural network learn how to tell the difference, between an image she recognizes and one she doesn't. For this one i got the fashionmnist dataset. Again i used holdout for separate the dataset 80/10/10. The model compression is from 748 to 32 dimensions.

lstm.title: LSTM Neural Network
lstm.desc: On LSTM i desing a price estimator for bitcoin price. I used the bitcoin historic price change, but i only took data from 2023 onwards. Why? Because my experiment was taking more than 6 hours to complete. And yes using the VGA on google colab. I normalizes the atributes using the z-score, because is (as far as I know) the best way to normalize without experiencing significant fluctuations in the data's means and standard deviations, and without the data being influenced by extreme variations.

f1_vrum.title: F1 vrum-vrum
f1_vrum.desc: An API built using FastAPI. The project aims to create an API featuring Formula 1 season data. It will allow users to query drivers, teams, circuits, races, seasons, and results. Planned future features include predictions, statistics, and a dashboard.

ecommerce.title: Gaming E-commerce
ecommerce.desc: I built a full-stack e-commerce platform using AdonisJS, which runs on Node.js. The platform is a game store following the MVC pattern that supports various platforms ranging from PC to PS5. The backend was built as a REST API featuring authentication, session management, and database management (using SQLite). Database operations were handled via an ORM (including migrations and seeders), and the RAWG API was used to populate the data. Project features include CRUD functionality for users and items (with an admin dashboard), a wishlist, and a commenting system. Additionally, the project implements debouncing and pagination for database queries, shopping cart persistence, and integration with the Stripe payment gateway.

comp_prog.title: Competitive Programming & Algorithms
comp_prog.desc: Refers to my study and projects focused on algorithms, which led me to prepare for programming marathons. Also includes solutions for several LeetCode problems.

research.title: LLMs, economics and BigFive
research.desc: For my capstone project, I conducted research integrating Computer science, economics, and psychology. The goal was to use LLMs to simulate decision-making and analyze their strategies, specifically examining how variations across the Big Five personality spectrum and macroeconomic contexts influence those decisions.

about_me.title: A Little About Me
about_me.subtitle: A Little About My Learning Journey
about_me.desc: During university, I began my studies with C. Later, while studying OOP, I learned core concepts using JAVA, covering polymorphism, inheritance, and encapsulation. I also studied C++ for competitive programming. As shown in the portfolio, I have used TypeScript to build an e-commerce with NodeJS (using agents). Currently, I am focusing more on Python, Golang, and SQL—practicing hands-on skills, modeling, and queries—to pursue my desired career path in Data Science / MLOps. I use Linux on my laptop for programming and learning, including Docker, terminal usage, and more. During college, I also focused my studies on artificial intelligence, covering subjects such as AI, machine learning, data mining, neural networks, natural language processing, and recommendation systems. Now, I am exploring a different area: software engineering and architecture. To finish, i'm studying system desing.
